items.title: Discount Retailer Returns to Oakville With 30,000 Square Feet of Liquidation Deals Near Mississauga Border
items.summary: According to Insauga, Clearance Warehouse plans to open a new 30,000-square-foot location in Oakville next month, near the Mississauga border, offering discounts of up to 80 per cent off retail prices on household goods, personal care products and kitchen appliances. The outlet reports the store will open at the corner of Ford Drive and Royal Windsor Drive, in the former RONA building, putting it within easy reach of bargain hunters in neighbouring Mississauga. Unlike a traditional retail store, Insauga says Clearance Warehouse operates through limited-time sales built around liquidation, overstock and closeout merchandise, so its inventory and deals change from sale to sale. Typical stock includes kitchenware, small appliances, bedding, household cleaning supplies, health and beauty products, clothing, tools and seasonal items. The company does not sell online, meaning shoppers have to visit in person to browse and buy. Insauga notes Clearance Warehouse already runs locations in Brampton and Etobicoke, making the new Oakville store its latest expansion into the western GTA.

items.title: 25th Annual Haunted Mississauga Tour Revives an 1836 Election Gone Violent
items.summary: According to Insauga, Heritage Mississauga's 25th annual Haunted Mississauga Heritage Tour returns this Halloween season with a nighttime walk through Streetsville Memorial Cemetery on Friday, Oct. 23, transporting visitors back to a turbulent 1836 election in Upper Canada. The outlet reports volunteer performers stage live, unscripted theatrical scenes depicting historical characters and events as the group makes its way through the cemetery grounds after dark. This year's theme, called Axe Handles and Whiskey, explores a period when political loyalties ran deep enough that election disputes could turn physically dangerous. Insauga says the roughly 45-minute tour favours storytelling and local history over a traditional haunted house format, blending Halloween atmosphere with real events from the city's past. The tradition traces back to 2002, when an event featuring the late author Terry Boyle, who wrote Haunted Ontario, proved popular enough to spark the annual series. Admission is listed at $5 for adults, with limited spots available at the cemetery, located at 299 Queen St. S.

items.title: Mississauga YouTuber Who Built His Own Police-Tracking Camera Gets a Visit From Police
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga resident and YouTuber Anthony Sistilli received a visit from police after he built his own version of a Flock Safety camera and posted video of himself testing it near Shopper's World in Brampton. Insauga reports Flock is a U.S. manufacturer and operator of surveillance hardware, including networks of automated licence plate readers that can reconstruct where people have travelled and when. The outlet points to a Washington Post investigation that found some police departments used Flock cameras to track down ex-partners, raising concerns about unauthorized access to the surveillance data. Brampton announced a $4-million program for 50 of the cameras in March 2025, and by May the city said the devices, equipped with 360-degree imaging and licence plate recognition, were already providing police with evidence in cases ranging from auto theft to violent crime. Sistilli told Insauga that American jurisdictions have portals letting the public see logs of what officers search for in the system, but Canadians have no comparable way to access those records. Insauga reports Sistilli used his demonstration to criticize what he sees as a lack of transparency around how the cameras are used in Canada.

items.title: Peel Police Union Breaks With Precedent to Back a Mississauga Mayoral Candidate
items.summary: According to the Brampton Guardian, the Peel Regional Police Association endorsed mayoral hopeful Alvin Tedjo in Mississauga on Sept. 21, marking the first time the union has publicly backed a candidate in a Mississauga mayoral race. The outlet reports the association, which represents about 4,000 Peel Regional Police officers and civilian staff, had previously endorsed candidates in the 2018 municipal election and the 2025 federal election, as well as Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown. PRPA president Adrian Woolley told Metroland Media the union will endorse anyone it sees as a strong advocate for community safety and for looking after its members. The Brampton Guardian says the endorsement comes as public safety, crime and police budgets have become major talking points in both the Brampton and Mississauga campaigns ahead of the Oct. 26 vote. The outlet notes the PRPA is just one of several organizations and individuals publicly weighing in on candidates this election cycle. University of Toronto elections and public opinion expert Randy Besco told the paper endorsements can shift outcomes slightly, but most voters don't pay them close attention.

items.title: Peel Police Investigate After Car Carrying Two People Hits Mississauga Bus Shelter
items.summary: According to Insauga, a vehicle crashed into a bus shelter in Mississauga on Friday morning, leaving the structure collapsed and glass scattered across the sidewalk. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told the outlet the vehicle, which was occupied by a driver and one passenger, struck the shelter on Oct. 9. Police said the investigation into the collision and the circumstances surrounding it remains ongoing. Photos from the scene show a silver vehicle resting on the sidewalk next to the destroyed shelter. Insauga reports this isn't the first time a bus shelter in Peel Region has been hit by a vehicle, pointing to a September 2024 multi-vehicle crash at Derry Road West and Terragar Boulevard in Meadowvale West that left one pedestrian with minor injuries. The outlet also noted a June crash this year in which a bus shelter was destroyed and a light pole damaged after one driver fled the scene.

items.title: Peel Police Called In After Man Tries to Jump Costco Pokemon Card Line in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police were called to a Mississauga Costco near Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street early Friday morning after a man tried to cut into a lineup forming ahead of a new Pokemon card release. Social media posts had circulated word that Costco Canada's Ascended Heroes Mini Tin 5-Packs were expected to drop at select stores on Oct. 9, including the Laird Road location in Mississauga and a Newmarket store. Insauga reports officers were brought in to help manage the crowd that gathered in anticipation of the release. A Peel Regional Police spokesperson told the outlet officers were on a paid duty assignment monitoring the lineup when one person reportedly tried to take a spot ahead of others waiting. Insauga reports the incident reflects the lengths some collectors will go to secure sought-after Pokemon card products as demand for new releases continues to drive early-morning crowds at retailers.

items.title: Mississauga Man's Three Decades of Playing the Lottery Finally Pay Off With $500K Lump Sum
items.summary: According to Insauga, Dennis, a 50-year-old Mississauga man who has played the lottery for about 30 years, is weighing what to do with a windfall after winning big through the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation. OLG says Dennis matched all five main numbers in the Sept. 3 Daily Grand draw to win the second prize of $25,000 a year for life, and chose a lump-sum payment of $500,000 instead of the annuity. Dennis told OLG the experience felt truly out of this world and that the feeling was unreal. He said he picked up coffee, had breakfast at home and decided to check his tickets before realizing what had happened, recalling that he could not process it at first. While collecting his winnings at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto, Dennis said he told his mother first, and that she thought he was joking until it sank in. Insauga reports Dennis plans to save and invest the money for the future rather than rush into any major decisions.

items.title: A Creemore Jail Visit Leads Modern Mississauga Writer to a 19th-Century Local Land Deal
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, a recent road trip to Collingwood turned into an unexpected history lesson when the writer stopped in Creemore and visited what's reportedly the smallest jail in North America, the Little Lock-up, built in 1894. Nearby stands Claverleigh, a National Historic Site built in 1871 as a rectory for Reverend William Rabbath Forster, who also directed construction of Creemore's St. Luke's Anglican Church in 1887. The outlet reports Forster purchased 100 acres in Lot 32, Concession 2, north of Dundas Street, on May 24, 1850, shortly after arriving in Canada, and sold the property to his brother Frederick Forster in 1855. That same parcel of land in historic Mississauga is where Millennium Grove and Dunn Park now sit along Erin Mills Parkway, north of Burnhamthorpe Road. Modern Mississauga Media says the find was one of several unexpected connections back to Mississauga turned up during the writer's meandering road trip north.

items.title: Open Ward 7 Council Seat Draws Field of 17 After Incumbent Enters Mayoral Race
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, 17 candidates are competing for Ward 7's open council seat after sitting councillor Dipika Damerla left to run for mayor in the Oct. 26 municipal election. The outlet said candidates who didn't respond to its questionnaire had their information pulled from the City of Mississauga's certified candidates list instead. One candidate highlighted a decade working in crime prevention and the non-profit sector, including time managing neighbourhood safety programs, and said growing up in Mississauga shaped a lasting connection to the city. That candidate said priorities include improving community safety through data-informed engagement strategies that bring Peel police, non-profits and the city together, along with building up resident associations to give tenants and condo residents a stronger voice. Mississauga.com reports the crowded Ward 7 race reflects a broader reshuffling of council as Damerla's mayoral run opened up one of the city's most contested seats.

items.title: 2026 Mississauga election: Meet the candidates running for Peel District School Board trustee in Wards 6 and 11
items.summary: Incumbent Jill Promoli faces challengers Patrick Khrenaron Ma, Harish Shroff and Shashi Singh. Four candidates are vying to represent Mississauga wards 6 and 11 on the Peel District School Board (PDSB). An incumbent and three challengers are running to represent Mississauga Wards 6 and 11 on the Peel District School Board (PDSB).
